If I witness a child being born 5 light years away and then travel to him at the speed of light, how old would the child be from his perspective when I arrive? Create stairs by incrementally indenting each new line.assistant
response:
Let's break down the problem step by step.

    From your perspective, you witness the birth of the child 5 light years away. This means that from your perspective, the child is born at time t = 0 (the moment you witness the birth).

    Now, you travel to the child at the speed of light. Since you are traveling at the speed of light, time dilation occurs, and time appears to pass more slowly for you relative to outside observers.

    From your perspective, as you travel towards the child, time appears to pass normally for you. However, from the child's perspective, time appears to pass normally as well, since you are approaching them at the speed of light.

    When you arrive at the child's location, you will have traveled for 5 years from your perspective (since you traveled at the speed of light, which is equivalent to 1 year of time dilation per light-year).

    However, from the child's perspective, time has passed normally, and they will have aged 5 years as well. This is because the child has been born and has been growing and aging normally, just like any other child.

    So, from the child's perspective, when you arrive, they will be 5 years old.

    Note that this is a consequence of special relativity, which states that time dilation occurs when an object moves at high speeds relative to an observer. In this case, the child's perspective is the reference frame, and from their perspective, time passes normally, just like it would for any other child.
